- Baseline MaxVehicles = 4.
- During I1 (ticks 4-15 inclusive), effective MaxVehicles = floor(4 × 0.5) = 2.

Suppose at tick 5, there are already 2 vehicles on E9. A third vehicle at N4 requests ENTER_EDGE(E9):
- In the Capacity & Conflict Check Phase, approving this would exceed MaxVehicles = 2.
- The request is denied; the vehicle instead performs WAIT at N4 for that tick.

skill_drafts.name: Incident Capacity Reduction Enforcement
skill_drafts.description: Computes an edge's effective MaxVehicles under an active incident's CapacityMultiplier and enforces that limit during the Capacity & Conflict Check Phase, denying ENTER_EDGE requests that would exceed it. Use when an incident reduces edge capacity and a vehicle requests entry.
skill_drafts.objective: Compute effective edge capacity under an incident and deny entry requests that would exceed it.
applicable_signals: Active incident with CapacityMultiplier on the target edge
ENTER_EDGE request targeting an edge with reduced capacity
Current occupancy at or near effective MaxVehicles
contraindications: No incident is active on the edge
The request is not an edge-entry request
intervention_moves: Derive baseline MaxVehicles from LaneCount and CapacityPerLane
Apply floor(baseline × CapacityMultiplier) to get effective MaxVehicles
Compare current occupancy plus requested vehicle against effective MaxVehicles
Deny over-capacity ENTER_EDGE and substitute WAIT at current node
workflow_steps: Identify the active incident and its CapacityMultiplier on the target edge.
On an ENTER_EDGE request, check whether occupancy plus the new vehicle exceeds effective MaxVehicles.
If it would exceed, deny the request and have the vehicle WAIT at its current node for that tick; otherwise approve.
triggers: An active incident specifies a CapacityMultiplier on an edge
A vehicle requests ENTER_EDGE on an edge with reduced capacity
constraints: Apply the floor function to the capacity product.
Enforce the limit only during the Capacity & Conflict Check Phase.
Denied vehicles must WAIT at their current node for that tick.
cautions: Do not apply the multiplier when no incident is active on the edge.
Do not approve entry that would push occupancy above effective MaxVehicles.
output_contract: Effective MaxVehicles computed and over-capacity ENTER_EDGE requests denied, with denied vehicles performing WAIT at their current node.

examples.input: Incident I1 on an edge with LaneCount = 2, CapacityPerLane = 2, CapacityMultiplier = 0.5; at a tick, 2 vehicles already on the edge and a third requests ENTER_EDGE.
examples.output: Baseline MaxVehicles = 4; effective MaxVehicles = floor(4 × 0.5) = 2; request denied; vehicle performs WAIT at its current node for that tick.
examples.notes: Illustrates incident-driven capacity math and admission denial.

metadata.prompt: During the Capacity & Conflict Check Phase, for an edge with an active incident specifying a CapacityMultiplier: (1) take the edge's baseline MaxVehicles (LaneCount × CapacityPerLane); (2) compute effective MaxVehicles = floor(baseline × CapacityMultiplier); (3) when a vehicle requests ENTER_EDGE, approve only if current occupancy plus the new vehicle does not exceed effective MaxVehicles; otherwise deny the request and have the vehicle perform WAIT at its current node for that tick.

skill_drafts.name: Over-Capacity Entry Denial with WAIT Fallback
skill_drafts.description: Resolve an edge-entry capacity conflict deterministically: when approving an ENTER_EDGE request would push an edge above its effective MaxVehicles, deny the request and assign the vehicle a WAIT action at its current node for that tick. Use during the capacity and conflict check phase when a vehicle is queued at a node to enter a full edge.
skill_drafts.objective: Deny over-capacity entry and substitute a WAIT action for the tick.
applicable_signals: Approving an ENTER_EDGE would exceed MaxVehicles
A vehicle is waiting at a node to enter a full edge
Edge occupancy already equals effective MaxVehicles
contraindications: Vehicle is not requesting edge entry
intervention_moves: Compute effective MaxVehicles for the target edge (baseline adjusted by active incident multiplier)
Compare current occupancy plus the requesting vehicle against effective MaxVehicles
Deny the ENTER_EDGE request when it would exceed the limit
Assign WAIT at the vehicle's current node for that tick
workflow_steps: Determine the target edge's effective MaxVehicles, applying any active incident CapacityMultiplier with floor.
Check current occupancy of the edge plus the requesting vehicle against effective MaxVehicles.
If the request would exceed MaxVehicles, deny the ENTER_EDGE request.
Assign the vehicle a WAIT action at its current node for that tick.
If the request would not exceed MaxVehicles, allow normal admission (out of scope for this skill).
triggers: An ENTER_EDGE request would exceed the edge's effective MaxVehicles
A vehicle is waiting at a node to enter a full edge
Capacity and conflict check phase is evaluating an edge-entry request
constraints: Denial must be based on the effective MaxVehicles, not the baseline, when an incident is active.
The denied vehicle must receive a WAIT action for the tick; it must not be left actionless.
Apply the check within the Capacity & Conflict Check Phase.
cautions: Ensure the incident CapacityMultiplier is applied with floor before comparing occupancy.
Do not admit a vehicle that would exceed the limit even if it is the only pending request.
output_contract: Entry denied and vehicle assigned WAIT at its node for the tick.

examples.input: Incident I1 on E9 (N4 to N9) with CapacityMultiplier = 0.5; baseline LaneCount = 2, CapacityPerLane = 2, baseline MaxVehicles = 4; effective MaxVehicles = floor(4 × 0.5) = 2. At tick 5, 2 vehicles already on E9; a third vehicle at N4 requests ENTER_EDGE(E9).
examples.output: Request denied; the vehicle performs WAIT at N4 for that tick.

metadata.prompt: During the Capacity & Conflict Check Phase, evaluate each ENTER_EDGE request against the target edge's effective MaxVehicles (baseline LaneCount × CapacityPerLane, adjusted by any active incident CapacityMultiplier via floor). If approving the request would exceed MaxVehicles, deny the entry and assign the vehicle WAIT at its current node for that tick. Do not admit the vehicle and do not leave it without an action for the tick.
